front: Direct vs. indirect costs of control
back:
Direct: out-of-pocket (e.g. audit staff, systems).
Indirect: behavioural displacement, gamesmanship, operating delays, negative attitudes.
Control system encourages behaviour inconsistent with objectives – people optimize what is measured, not what matters.
Actions to improve measured indicators without real positive effects – slack creation, data manipulation.
